name: Starter Labs applicant-stage aggregate

attribution.legal_posture: Starter Labs' CEO told the South China Morning Post that the company received 47 applicants in one month whom he described as North Korean and hired none. This is the executive's reported assessment; DPRK-national count, government finding, legal-identity determination, and independent verification require separate evidence.

caveats: Appearance, accent, nationality, ethnicity, language, geography, remote-work preference, camera behavior, VPN use, and any single device or network signal require corroboration before attribution.

The executive's assessment concerns 47 applicants or workers in the reported context; that assessment remains distinct from 47 confirmed DPRK nationals or government-attributed workers.
This record covers the aggregate finding; applicant identity, current account, private identity, address, contact detail, and technical selector remain outside it.
The reported assessment reaches the applicant stage. Access, compromise, and malicious conduct belong to later evidentiary questions.
This record identifies, retains, or infers no applicant, worker, identity-theft victim, current account, private data, victim data, indicator, contact value, or technical selector.

sources.support: Provenance: The article directly interviews Starter Labs founder and CEO Marlon Williams about applications received by his own software-development company. Williams said the company received 47 applicants in one month whom he described as North Korean. He said none were hired and described the volume as part of a recurring applicant-fraud problem affecting his startup. Normalized boundary: Starter Labs' CEO said the software-development startup received 47 applicants in one month whom he described as North Korean and hired none of them. Attribution boundary: Named executive's assessment reported in an original interview; not a government finding, court determination, or independently verified count of DPRK nationals. Publication boundary: Applicant-stage aggregate only. Do not identify candidates, treat all 47 as legally confirmed DPRK workers, or infer access, compromise, or a successful hire
